Data handling

Source: DATA_HANDLING.md

tidycreel.connect is a connector package. It reads an agency’s creel data at run time, through a connection the user supplies (CSV paths, a DBI database or a REST API). It stores no survey data of its own.

Where sensitive data lives

Data Location (outside this repo) Contains PII? Custodian
Agency creel interviews, counts, catch and lengths The agency’s database or API, reached through creel_connect() / creel_connect_api() Possibly (e.g. angler ZIP code, interviewer names) The agency data steward
Shipped fixture: inst/extdata/synthetic-boat-counts/counts.csv In this repo (whitelisted in .gitignore) No: synthetic daily aggregate counts Package maintainer

PII never enters this repository. Test fixtures are synthetic, built in test helpers or written to tempdir(), and never copied from an agency extract.

What analysts receive

  • The fetch functions return what the connection is mapped to carry. Map only the fields an analysis needs; unmapped columns are dropped.
  • Quasi-identifiers such as zip_code are summarised (by ZIP or county), not reported row by row.
  • Small cells are suppressed per agency policy before results leave the secure environment.

Credentials

  • Never written in code or in a committed YAML profile. Profiles read them with !expr, from the OS keyring (keyring::key_get()) or the environment (Sys.getenv()).
  • For an API token, prefer a function that looks it up at request time, e.g. token: !expr function() keyring::key_get("creel-api"). A token given as a string is held in the connection object: print() hides it, but str(), dput(), saveRDS(), save() and a saved .RData workspace all write it out (checked 2026-10-28). A function that looks the token up keeps it out of all of them. A function that returns a token variable does not help: made inside another function or local(), the variable is saved with the function; made at top level, it stays in the workspace and a saved .RData holds it.
  • Never save a connection object to disk, and do not save the workspace on exit in a session that holds one. Save the fetched data and reconnect.
  • Print methods never show a password or token; keep it that way.
  • Use read-only database accounts.
  • A credential that appears in a commit, log, or chat transcript is treated as compromised and rotated.

Profiles are code

A YAML profile is evaluated by config, which runs every !expr value as R with the user’s permissions, credentials and data access. Read a profile you did not write before loading it, and never load one from a source you would not run code from. Share the non-secret parts of a profile (endpoints, field names, table names); each user keeps the secrets in their own keyring or environment.

Data in transit

  • API connections use https:// and send requests, next pages and redirects only to the origin of base_url, so a token cannot reach another server (#30). Plain http:// to a non-loopback host needs allow_http = TRUE and warns.
  • SQL Server profiles connect with Driver 18, encrypted, verifying the server’s certificate (#31). Turning either protection off warns on every connect.
  • A connection built by hand with DBI::dbConnect() is the user’s own: set Encrypt there yourself.

Safeguards in this repo

  • .gitignore is deny-by-default for data formats and credential files; the one shipped fixture is whitelisted by path.
  • Local pre-commit hook (pii-guard + gitleaks) blocks staged PII and secrets. It is per clone: run install_precommit.sh from pii-guard after cloning.
  • Code that touches PII is developed against synthetic data.

If something leaks

Follow the pii-guard sandbox remediation protocol: back up, rewrite history in a throwaway clone, verify with count-only checks, force-push, clean the server, realign local copies, rotate any exposed credential.
